name: consumer-smoke
comment: Every @elabs-ai/components-* version below is a PLACEHOLDER. check-consumer-install.mjs
rewrites each one to a file: reference pointing at a freshly packed tarball,
then installs this app OUTSIDE the workspace. Do not add real ranges here
-- that instruction is scoped to the @elabs-ai/components-* entries only.
@xyflow/react, monaco-editor and maplibre-gl below are DIFFERENT: they are
each package's own SDK/engine peerDependency, pinned to a real, current
version on purpose (issue #41). Nothing else in this fixture's install graph
declares a competing version of those three, so pnpm's auto-install-peers
(.npmrc: strict-peer-dependencies=true, set below by check-consumer-install.mjs)
would otherwise silently satisfy a narrowed/wrong peer range from thin air --
a #30-shaped regression could ship undetected. Keep these real; do not
genericize them back to "*".
pnpm.peerDependencyRules.allowedVersions below is a SEPARATE, narrowly-scoped
exemption -- not a relaxation of the strict-peer-dependencies=true check above.
@visx/brush@3.12.0 (a transitive dep of @elabs-ai/components-charts) still
declares its own react peer at ^16-18 and pulls @visx/drag/@visx/group/@visx/shape
at the same old major, all with the same stale peer range -- a pre-existing,
already-tolerated gap (this repo's own root .npmrc sets
strict-peer-dependencies=false for exactly this reason) that is UNRELATED to the
@xyflow/react / monaco-editor / maplibre-gl peers this fixture exists to guard.
Each entry is scoped to one requester>react pair so a real regression on any of
the three SDK peers above -- or on react itself for any @elabs-ai/components-*
package -- still fails strict-peer-dependencies. Do not widen this to a bare
"react" key; that would silently swallow the class of regression this fixture
was built to catch.
